hallucinations.claim: In December 2025 the average price was $4.25 per dozen, a 60% jump from a year earlier
hallucinations.why: That is the December 2022 figure from the CBS 2022 article; December 2025 was nowhere near $4.25 and prices were falling, not up 60%.

hallucinations.claim: a year before that ... roughly $2.66 per dozen; compared to a year ago, the price has fallen from about $2.66 to $2.25 (≈15% lower)
hallucinations.why: BLS September 2025 was $3.49 and September 2026 $2.27, so the drop is ~35%; the $2.66 baseline is derived from a misdated 2022 figure.

hallucinations.claim: the price for that month [September 2026] isn't listed in the data I have
hallucinations.why: The FRED series page it cited carries the September 2026 value ($2.27); the answer apologises for missing data that existed.

what_went_wrong: Search found the right FRED series but the read stage did not extract the September 2026 value, and the draft misdated a 2022 CBS article as December 2025; the reviewer flagged the date but the fix produced a wrong year-ago figure and wrong 15% change.
great_answer_would: Say $2.27 a dozen in September 2026 vs $3.49 in September 2025 (BLS/FRED APU0000708111), down ~35% as the 2025 bird-flu spike unwound.
notes: April 2026 $2.25 is plausible near the June low of $2.14 but is not the current figure; it points to the St. Louis Fed rather than BLS as the source.

hallucinations.why: Self-contradictory: by its own numbers driving is $540 cheaper. The reference verdict is roughly a wash on cash.

hallucinations.claim: the Brooklyn-to-Miami trip is ~1,080 miles ... ~2,160 mile round trip
hallucinations.why: The drive is ~1,280 miles each way.

hallucinations.claim: fuel at about $3.50 / gallon as of 2025
hallucinations.why: Stale (trap): October 2026 national average is ~$4.35-4.41, ~40% above a year ago; dated, but used as the current basis for the estimate.

hallucinations.claim: average round-trip domestic fare of $522 per person
hallucinations.why: A generic calculator average, not a NYC-MIA fare; Kayak shows $160-380 round trip, so $1,044 for two overstates flying badly.

hallucinations.claim: Driving also takes roughly 18 hours one way
hallucinations.why: ~19-20 hours of driving each way; minor understatement.

what_went_wrong: Search returned one generic calculator plus junk (Serengeti, Hotline Miami, OneDrive), so the writer used a national average fare and invented 2025 driving costs; the merge then stated a verdict that contradicts its own numbers, and the reviewer's notes were mostly dropped.
great_answer_would: Show two short cost stacks (drive ~$720-820 out of pocket with 2026 gas, tolls and two hotel nights, plus wear; fly ~$450-1,050 for two plus a ~$300-500 Miami rental) and call it a cash wash: fly unless you need the car.
notes: No tolls, hotel nights, Miami rental car or bags counted; the four lost travel days are mentioned only loosely.

hallucinations.why: Acela is ~3h35-3h50 and the Regional 4h-4h30; it understates the train time and does not tell the two services apart.

hallucinations.claim: Flights from NYC to Boston typically run $80–$150 one-way
hallucinations.why: Reference range is ~$100-320 one way plus $30-80 airport transit each way; understated, and it makes flying look cheaper than the train.

what_went_wrong: The read stage got 0 full pages (8 passages, an ad link and off-topic Europe/Barcelona pages), so time and cost figures came from model knowledge, and an invented diesel CO₂ claim survived review.
great_answer_would: Lead with the train, give Acela (~3h40, ~$85-230) vs Regional (~4h15, ~$30-130) vs flying (3.5-4+ h door to door, $100-320 plus airport transit) vs bus ($20-45), and name the one case for flying.

hallucinations.claim: Ollama is the faster runtime on a 48-GB M4 Pro for agent-level inference
hallucinations.why: Wrong central verdict (trap): MLX is faster, and Ollama 0.19 (Mar 2026) closed the gap by switching its Mac backend to MLX. The answer's own next sentence says MLX matched or beat Ollama.

hallucinations.claim: benchmarks report it running 70-B models at 'usable speeds' ... 70 B is the practical upper bound for a single-process inference run on a 48-GB M4 Pro
hallucinations.why: Trap: a 4-bit 70B (~40 GB) leaves no headroom on 48 GB and swaps; the realistic ceiling is ~30-35B 4-bit. This also contradicts the answer's own '32-B+ models quickly hit memory limits'.

hallucinations.claim: Qwen 3.5-A3B on an M4 Max found MLX delivering roughly twice the token-rate of Ollama (60-70 tok/s vs. ~35 tok/s)
hallucinations.why: The reference benchmark is ~132 vs ~48 tok/s on an M4 Max; the figures may come from [4] but are presented loosely and attributed to the wrong machine context.

what_went_wrong: The writer misread source [1] and put Ollama ahead; the reviewer flagged it, but the fix only bolted on a contradicting sentence, and the size paragraph merged incompatible claims (35B ceiling vs 70B upper bound). Nothing mentions Ollama 0.19's MLX backend.
great_answer_would: Say MLX is faster but Ollama 0.19+ now uses MLX on 32 GB+ Macs (check your version), give the 273 GB/s bandwidth rule (~15 tok/s for a 27B 4-bit, 60-100+ for 3B-active MoE), cap at ~30-35B 4-bit, and flag slow long-prompt prefill.
notes: The answer contradicts itself on both questions, so it gives Pat no usable verdict; nothing on long-context prefill.

hallucinations.claim: The systematic review that gathered 15 interventional studies—seven of which reported anxiety outcomes

hallucinations.claim: Magnesium taurate ... sometimes chosen when heart-related anxiety is a concern
hallucinations.why: No trial evidence for taurate in anxiety; presented as a co-equal recommendation alongside glycinate.

hallucinations.claim: doses above [350 mg] ... can cause diarrhea or low blood pressure
hallucinations.why: Above the UL the main effect is GI; hypotension is a toxicity sign at much higher doses or with kidney impairment, so this is mildly overstated.

what_went_wrong: Search found the right PMC reviews and the NIH UL, so the core is right, but the writer pulled in an off-topic PMS/B6 paragraph from a supplement blog, ended with a recap he asked not to get, and missed the kidney and label cautions.
great_answer_would: Give 200-400 mg elemental (glycinate or citrate, evening) in two sentences, say plainly the evidence is small and low-quality with no large RCT, then add the 'elemental vs compound weight on the label' and kidney-disease cautions.
notes: Dose, forms, the oxide caveat and the 350 mg UL are all correct, and calling the evidence 'modest' with heterogeneous trials is roughly right. The PMS paragraph is irrelevant to Pat, and the final recap paragraph breaks his preference.
